fields.sample_size: 80 local-government submissions on the Water Services Entities Bill 2022 (all 67 territorial authorities and 11 regional councils, plus two further submissions as published on the NZ Parliament website); supplementary newspaper, media and council reports reviewed but not coded
fields.study_design: qualitative thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke six phases, NVivo) of local-government submissions, structured with the OECD Water Governance Framework
fields.effect_estimate: Councils' submissions raised major concerns about loss of local voice and accountability, affordability, and the complexity of the proposed governance structures, while generally acknowledging the importance of mana whenua participation in decisions and supporting the independent regulator Taumata Arowai. Qualitative; no effect estimate.
fields.section: Full text: Abstract; 2 Methodology (2.1 data sources and scope, 2.2 analytical approach); Results; Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a thematic analysis of 80 local-government submissions on New Zealand's Water Services Entities Bill 2022 found concerns about lost local voice, accountability and affordability, with support for mana whenua participation and the independent regulator Taumata Arowai; qualitative, read in full text 2026-10-04.
pdf_note: Water Policy 27(12) 2025 article (Drive file R21EB956A971B), about 80,000 characters of converted text read; tables skimmed
notes: The first extraction described the case in general terms with no sample; the full text gives 80 submissions (67 territorial authorities and 11 regional councils named). The documents analysed are council submissions, not respondents.
